nodes.label: Halveti-Jerrahi
nodes.blurb: Sufi order founded in Istanbul by Nureddin Cerrahi (1704), a branch of the Halveti (Khalwati); carried to North America by Muzaffer Ozak from 1980.

nodes.label: Jewish Renewal
nodes.blurb: Movement begun by Rabbi Zalman Schachter-Shalomi that brings Hasidic and Kabbalistic contemplative practice into an egalitarian, ecumenical Judaism; close to Neo-Hasidism.

nodes.label: Integral Yoga (Sri Aurobindo and the Mother)
nodes.blurb: Sri Aurobindo and the Mother's yoga of transformation (Puducherry, Auroville): not Swami Satchidananda's Integral Yoga.

nodes.label: Integral Yoga (Swami Satchidananda)
nodes.blurb: Swami Satchidananda's synthesis of hatha, raja, bhakti, karma, jnana and japa yoga (Integral Yoga Institutes, Yogaville); he was a disciple of Swami Sivananda. Not Sri Aurobindo's Integral Yoga.

nodes.label: Nichiren Buddhism
nodes.blurb: Japanese schools founded on Nichiren's (1222-1282) teaching of the Lotus Sutra and the chanting of its title, Nam-myoho-renge-kyo.

nodes.label: Soka Gakkai
nodes.blurb: Lay Nichiren Buddhist movement founded in Japan in 1930; Soka Gakkai International (SGI) has national organisations worldwide (SGI-UK: Taplow Court).
